candidate_contract: Nine source-only candidates preserve the same candidate IDs and primitive sequences used by the unchanged exact-sequence transfer baseline. R4 outcomes do not alter candidate IDs, sequences, ranking priors or thresholds.

candidates.mechanism: Cache the loaded core image and band count, then replace the explicit empty-list plus append loop with one list comprehension before the existing tuple return.
candidates.source_visible_precondition: Image.split builds an empty Python list, repeatedly appends one wrapped getband result, then converts that list to a tuple.
candidates.correctness_risk: low: preserve getband order, _new wrapping, single-band semantics and final tuple type.
candidates.expected_performance_mechanism: reduce Python bytecode dispatch and repeated append-method work while executing the same per-band core operations.

candidates.mechanism: After split has already loaded the image, execute a direct core copy for the one-band path with self._new(self.im.copy()); certify the one-band condition first and retain self.copy() only as a compatibility recovery if direct core copy is unavailable.
candidates.source_visible_precondition: Image.split calls self.load() before branching, while Image.copy immediately calls self.load() again and then returns self._new(self.im.copy()).
candidates.correctness_risk: low_to_medium: the recovery must preserve subclasses or unusual core objects that do not expose copy exactly as expected.
candidates.expected_performance_mechanism: avoid a redundant Python method call and second load() dispatch on the one-band path while preserving copy semantics.

candidates.mechanism: Certify the one-band case immediately after load and return (self.copy(),) directly; recover to the existing multiband construction only when band count is greater than one.
candidates.source_visible_precondition: The current one-band branch allocates a one-element list and then converts it to a tuple even though the final shape is known exactly.
candidates.correctness_risk: low: identical one-band copy object and one-element tuple must be returned.
candidates.expected_performance_mechanism: remove list allocation and tuple conversion on one-band images.

candidates.mechanism: Specialize the common three-band and four-band cases into direct tuple construction with fixed getband indices, then execute the generic loop only for uncommon band counts.
candidates.source_visible_precondition: Image modes visible in the same source include common RGB/YCbCr/LAB/HSV three-band and RGBX/RGBA/CMYK four-band representations, while split currently uses a generic Python loop for every multiband count.
candidates.correctness_risk: low_to_medium: specialization must dispatch only by actual core band count and preserve exact ordering.
candidates.expected_performance_mechanism: avoid range iteration, list allocation and append dispatch for common 3/4-band images.

candidates.mechanism: Represent self.im, self._new and the loaded band count as local variables once, then execute the existing branch and loop through those locals.
candidates.source_visible_precondition: The loop repeatedly resolves self.im.getband and self._new through Python attribute lookup, and self.im.bands is read in both the branch and range setup.
candidates.correctness_risk: low: locals alias the same loaded objects without mutation.
candidates.expected_performance_mechanism: reduce repeated Python attribute and bound-method lookup overhead around each core getband call.

candidates.mechanism: Read self.im.bands once into a local band_count and reuse it for the one-band test and multiband iteration without changing collection construction.
candidates.source_visible_precondition: Image.split currently accesses self.im.bands once for equality and again to construct range().
candidates.correctness_risk: low: band count cannot lawfully change between those operations after load within split.
candidates.expected_performance_mechanism: remove one Python extension-object attribute access from every split call.

candidates.mechanism: Represent the loaded core image and wrapper constructor as locals, certify band_count > 1 after the one-band return, and restrict multiband construction to a fixed-size list comprehension over range(band_count) before tuple conversion.
candidates.source_visible_precondition: The multiband branch has an exact finite band count after load yet uses repeated object traversal and append growth.
candidates.correctness_risk: low: output remains an ordered tuple of _new(im.getband(i)) for every legal band index.
candidates.expected_performance_mechanism: combine local representation with bounded comprehension to reduce dynamic lookup and append overhead.

candidates.mechanism: Refine the one-band copy recovery by inlining Image.copy's post-load body as self._new(self.im.copy()) because split has already completed self.load().
candidates.source_visible_precondition: Image.copy consists of self.load() followed by self._new(self.im.copy()), and Image.split invokes self.load() before calling self.copy() in the one-band branch.
candidates.correctness_risk: low: must preserve _new metadata/palette propagation exactly.
candidates.expected_performance_mechanism: remove the redundant second load() dispatch and copy-method frame on one-band split.

candidates.mechanism: Represent im.getband and self._new as bound local callables and reduce the multiband loop to tuple(new(getband(i)) for i in range(band_count)), eliminating the explicit temporary list object.
candidates.source_visible_precondition: The final API requires a tuple, while the current implementation creates an intermediate list solely to populate it before tuple conversion.
candidates.correctness_risk: low: generator order and element construction must remain identical; performance may trade list allocation for generator overhead.
candidates.expected_performance_mechanism: remove the intermediate list allocation and repeated bound-method lookup, at the cost of generator dispatch that the evaluator will decide prospectively.
